xr27632.author: Plato
xr27632.label: All learning is recollection
xr27632.translation: The soul, then, as being immortal, and having been born again many times, and having seen all things that exist, whether in this world or in the world below, has knowledge of them all; and it is no wonder that she should be able to call to remembrance all that she ever knew about virtue, and about everything; for as all nature is akin, and the soul has learned all things; there is no difficulty in her eliciting or as men say learning, out of a single recollection all the rest, if a man is strenuous and does not faint; for all enquiry and all learning is but recollection.
xr27632.reading: Union is the end of the philosophical love affair, and it is not acquiring something new but remembering. Feeling a lack proves it: we would not suffer from the chains if we had not once been free, just as you cannot look for keys you do not know you lost.

wflzbp6.q: Have you ever hit rock bottom?

s1jxj8gd.title: The four Pythagorean principles
steps: Our nature and the divine essence are eternal: we are the One ('Unity is the law of God')
The One divides into parts, and from parts comes μοῖρα ('Number is the law of the universe')
Incarnating without παιδεία we drink Lethe, identify with the part, and suffer
There is a way out, the path of awakening ('Evolution is the law of life')
s1jxj8gd.note: A diagnosis and a cure: unity, division, forgetting, return.
